newsitem.title: UK: Italy becomes first country to raise debt in euros.
newsitem.headline: Italy becomes first country to raise debt in euros.

text.p: Italy has become the first sovereign borrower to raise funds in Europe's planned new single currency with a one billion euro issue launched on Tuesday, SBC Warburg said.

Other countries already have debt which may ultimately be repaid in euros after the third stage of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), but only because of clauses in the bond terms that allow repayment in the new currency.

Until the euro is introduced under EMU, all transactions in Italy's new seven-year euro bond will be made in Ecu, so the bond totals 1.0 billion Ecu ($1.15 billion). The bond was priced to yield 0.18 percentage points over an outstanding Ecu bond issued by France.
SBC Warburg acted as joint arranger of the issue with Paribas.
Italy is keen to be among the first nations adopting the euro, a move scheduled for January 1, 1999. But financial markets have doubts about its chances of meeting the qualifying criteria.
Austria and Portugal earlier this year both issued French franc bonds whose terms and conditions specifically allow for redenomination in euros after EMU.
Several quasi-state and corporate borrowers have also issued bonds in core-EMU currencies such as the French franc, guilder and mark.
Many countries have outstanding Ecu bonds dating back to the late 1980s which will also be redenominated after EMU.
